Eventually, the scheme collapses when there are no more new investors or when the promoter cannot continue to pay off existing investors. It is named after Charles Ponzi, who ran a similar scheme in the 1920s. To do a Ponzi scheme, you need to find people who are willing to invest their money with you and then convince them that you can provide them with high returns. You then use their money to pay off existing investors and create the illusion of profitability. Eventually, when there are no more new investors or when you cannot continue to pay off existing investors, the scheme will collapse.
